clue.text: The Head's unfeeling, we hear — stupid!

definitions.note: used as an exclamation calling someone a dunce, so it stands for the noun

indicators.note: the phrase tells us the clue words are to be spoken and the spelling taken from the sound

parts.note: a head that has no feeling is a numb skull

explanation.surface: Someone insults a headmaster as cold and dim.
explanation.walkthrough: The Head looks like a school head, but it is just the skull; 'numb skull' said quickly gives the spelling without the B.
explanation.definitionFit: A dunce or blockhead, the person you shout 'stupid!' at, is called a numskull.

clue.text: Uncivilized characters?

parts.note: characters, meaning dispositions, that are wild and untamed in the way that natural things are

explanation.definitionFit: A person's basic temperaments or dispositions, the untamed state before civilization.

clue.text: A prophet the heartless stone

parts.note: Malachi is the last of the minor prophets of the Old Testament

indicators.note: having no heart means the middle letter of the word is taken out

explanation.surface: A biblical prophet condemns the cruel stone.
explanation.walkthrough: 'heartless' looks like a description of the stone, but it removes the middle letter of THE, leaving TE.
explanation.definitionFit: A green copper mineral, polished as an ornamental gem.

clue.text: Marked a difficult wartime surrender

indicators.note: the letters are awkwardly placed, so they must be rearranged

explanation.surface: A hard surrender scored a mark on the war.
explanation.walkthrough: KAMERAD, German for comrade, was the call of a soldier giving himself up in the First World War.
explanation.definitionFit: German soldiers in the First World War cried 'comrade' in German when giving themselves up.

clue.text: Girl joins Baltic type on the rink

parts.note: a Lett is a person from Latvia, a Baltic state
a rink is a sheet of ice

explanation.surface: A girl goes skating with a Latvian.
explanation.definitionFit: A female first name, an old form of Letitia.

clue.text: Clock-watchers' bird, out on the hour

definitions.text: Clock-watchers' bird, out on the hour

parts.words: Clock-watchers' bird, out on the hour
parts.note: the little wooden bird that springs out of a Black Forest clock each hour to call the time

explanation.surface: Bored office workers watch a bird, longing to be out on the hour.
explanation.definitionFit: The bird in a novelty clock that pops out to mark each hour is named after the bird with the two-note call.

clue.text: Striking couples for dancing

parts.note: pairs of shells that are clacked together, struck in pairs, by Spanish dancers

explanation.definitionFit: Paired hollow shells of wood clicked together in the hand by flamenco dancers.

clue.text: City of spirit in Germany

parts.note: a German city that gave its name to a scented spirit, the toilet water first made there

explanation.definitionFit: The Rhineland city where eau de toilette was first made, so its name serves for the perfumed spirit.

clue.text: Take the upper bunk, when past 50, that is

parts.note: over means past, as in 'the danger is over'
L is the Roman numeral for fifty
i.e. is the abbreviation of id est, that is

explanation.surface: A man past fifty takes the top bunk.
explanation.walkthrough: 'when past 50' suggests age, but past is OVER and 50 the Roman L.
explanation.definitionFit: To lie on top of something, as one sleeper does above another.

clue.text: Recording transmitters — providing TAM-rating material ?

explanation.surface: Devices that send back readings supply the figures for television ratings.
explanation.walkthrough: TAM stood for Television Audience Measurement, the British TV ratings service of the time, which used meters fitted to sets in sample homes.
explanation.definitionFit: Instruments that measure at a distance and send their readings by radio; TAM's set meters were such devices, feeding the viewing figures.

clue.text: 25's emblem unpopular with sailors, we hear

definitions.note: 25 across is the Welshman, whose national emblem is a vegetable

indicators.note: this tells us to say the word that the clue words describe and write down a word of the same sound

parts.note: a hole letting water into a ship is the last thing a sailor wants

explanation.surface: Something to do with a national symbol is disliked by seamen.
explanation.walkthrough: The OCR added the clue number 9 in front; the page prints only '25's'. The leek is worn on St David's Day as the national emblem of Wales.
explanation.definitionFit: The onion-like vegetable is the traditional national symbol of Wales, alongside the daffodil.

clue.text: No doubt we're all in his bad book !

definitions.text: No doubt we're all in his bad book !

parts.words: No doubt we're all in his bad book !
parts.note: a heavenly clerk who writes down every person's sins and good deeds, so all of us appear among the bad entries

explanation.definitionFit: In religious tradition an angel keeps a register of each soul's deeds, good and bad, for the Day of Judgement.

clue.text: Slip end, twist around here

indicators.note: to twist the words is to wrench their letters into a new order, the anagram signal

explanation.surface: A spinner lets the end of the yarn slip and winds the twist round this rod.
explanation.walkthrough: 'twist' signals the anagram and also tells you what a spinner does: the thread is twisted and wound around the rod.
explanation.definitionFit: The rod on a spinning wheel round which the thread is wound as it is twisted.

clue.text: Filmed, giving somehow equal credit without it

indicators.note: somehow means the letters are put together in some new way
without means the letters of the last word are taken away from the pool

explanation.surface: A film was made, giving some sort of fair credit except for one detail.
explanation.walkthrough: Take IT out of EQUAL CREDIT and rearrange the rest; 'Filmed' means coated with a thin film, not shot by camera.
explanation.definitionFit: Covered with a thin hard coat of varnish, a glossy layer.

clue.text: Adam married ? That's wet !

parts.note: Adam Bede is the title hero of George Eliot's novel
to be married is to have wed

explanation.surface: Someone remarks that the first man has taken a wife, and calls it a soaking business.
explanation.walkthrough: Adam looks like the first man in Genesis, but he is George Eliot's carpenter Adam Bede, giving his surname.
explanation.definitionFit: Covered with drops of dew, so moistened.

clue.text: Funny saying such as Tom comes back with

definitions.text: Funny saying such as Tom comes back with

parts.words: Funny saying such as Tom comes back with
parts.note: a smart quip of the kind a quick-witted person retorts with

explanation.definitionFit: A clever, amusing remark, the sort of retort a wit makes.

clue.text: Introduction before making up application ?

parts.note: pre- is the prefix meaning before
make-up put on the skin is a face, as in 'putting one's face on'

explanation.surface: An opening comes before a job application is drawn up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'making up' looks like composing, but means cosmetics; the 'application' is the coat of make-up called a face.
explanation.definitionFit: An opening section of a book, setting out its purpose before the main text.

clue.text: Animal overturns car, takes the company on

indicators.note: something overturned is upside down, so in a down entry the word car is turned round

parts.note: taken as written
Co. is the abbreviation for company
taken as written

explanation.surface: A wild animal tips a car over and then takes on the firm.
explanation.definitionFit: A ringtailed North American mammal with a masked face.

clue.text: Shops around militantly for food for a long time?

explanation.definitionFit: Searches widely for provisions, as an army foraging party does; split into two words, the phrase means for ages.

clue.text: Book needs a sort of stapler

indicators.note: a sort of stapler means the letters of the word sorted into a new form

explanation.surface: A book has to be held together with some kind of office fastener.
explanation.definitionFit: A volume containing the Psalms, a book of the Bible arranged for worship.

clue.text: As Flora's Mr Finching contrived to do seven times

definitions.text: As Flora's Mr Finching contrived to do seven times

parts.words: As Flora's Mr Finching contrived to do seven times
parts.note: in Dickens's Little Dorrit, Flora Finching says her late husband asked for her hand seven times

explanation.definitionFit: To offer marriage, which the late Mr F did again and again before Flora accepted.

clue.text: Charms a stubborn creature up the street

parts.note: the mule is proverbially obstinate

indicators.note: in a down entry, up means the letters are read from bottom to top

explanation.surface: Charms lure an obstinate animal up the road.
explanation.definitionFit: Lucky tokens worn to ward off harm.

clue.text: Herr X, of ray fame

parts.note: the German physicist who discovered X-rays in 1895, as Herr, Mister, of the rays

explanation.definitionFit: Wilhelm Conrad, the German scientist who discovered X-rays, which bear his name in German.

clue.text: Round-table conference talk ?

parts.note: read 'round' as roundabout: talk that goes round and round the subject rather than to the point

explanation.definitionFit: Wordy, evasive speech that circles a point instead of making it, like talk at endless conferences.

clue.text: A medal for striking

explanation.definitionFit: Slang for a decoration such as a military award; also a metal disc that rings when hit with a padded stick.

clue.text: Circle again around the bay for rescue work

indicators.note: the circling piece is laid around the bay, holding it within its letters

parts.note: to ring again is to re-ring
a cove is a small bay

explanation.surface: A ship circles once more round the inlet to carry out a rescue.
explanation.definitionFit: Salvage, the work of getting back a lost ship or cargo, is called getting it back.

clue.text: United Nations American news man is not employed

parts.note: US stands for American, as in United States
an editor, ED, is a newspaper man

explanation.surface: A UN reporter from the States finds himself out of work.
explanation.definitionFit: Idle, not in use, the state of something lying spare.

clue.text: Chap in a plaid

parts.note: Plaid here is Plaid Cymru, the Welsh nationalist party, so a man in it is from Wales

explanation.definitionFit: A man from Wales, the country of the party called Plaid Cymru.
